rationale:
Evidence: iteration 0 (kp 3.5, kd 0.15, ki 0.05, base 1.5, 12 mm sensors at y=0.06, last_direction) is still the best design at 53.02. Every run in every iteration ended off track at progress 0.04 to 0.15. The s-bend progress stayed at exactly 0.1475 across kp 3.5 to 4.5, base_speed 1.3 to 1.6 and both sensor sizes. Iteration 3 (kp 2.5) cut it to 0.043, so the s-bend is not fully insensitive to the controller, and iteration 2 (16 mm sensors) lowered the score to 50.49.

What I kept, changed and rejected after the round-2 critique:
(1) Kept the single-factor change from my revision: kd 0.15 to 0.4. Everything else equals iteration 0 (geometry, kp 3.5, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.5, weights [1, 0.5, 0, -0.5, -1], line_loss last_direction).
(2) Partly accepted the critique that the s-bend plateau argues against kd. The earlier kd values (0.2 with ki 0.4 in iteration 1, and the lumped changes) were confounded, so the plateau does not show kd is inert alone. Kd is the one controller term never tested by itself, so a clean test is still informative. I do not claim it will change the s-bend.
(3) Accepted the noise concern. Per-step signal changes multiplied by 100 per second and by kd 0.4 can produce a derivative term comparable to kp times the signal, so kd 0.4 is a real risk to steering jitter. I keep it as a test, with steering_oscillation as a watched measurement. If oscillation rises well above the baseline 0.10 to 0.14 range, that is evidence of noise amplification and the result is reverted.
(4) Accepted that the 0.05 score band is too narrow. Oval seed spread is 48 to 75, so I judge the result on per-track progress first, and on the three-track mean only when the change exceeds about 1 point.
(5) Rejected kd 1.2 from the round-1 draft and the base_speed change, which remain untested alone and would confound this race. Kept base_speed at 1.5, since no evidence shows speed is the limit.

Expected result: progress on at least one track rises above its iteration 0 value (s-bend above 0.1475 or oval above 0.1355) with steering_oscillation no more than about 1.5 times baseline. Decision rules: (a) if progress rises on at least two tracks, keep kd 0.4. (b) If progress is unchanged within 0.01 on all tracks and the score is within about 1 point of 53.0, damping is not the limit, and the next single test is base_speed alone (1.5 to 1.3 or 1.7). (c) If the score falls more than 1 point or oscillation rises sharply, revert kd to 0.15. (d) If progress exceeds 0.9 with completion 0, raise base_speed by 0.1. (e) If line_loss_events exceeds 2, test search_right alone.
